A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PT construction and interval-stability diagnostic. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments, regression and ImageNet classification evaluations, group-coverage analyses, stability measurements, and parameter ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds localized-CP stability measurements, relaxed-PT and stronger-bias experiments, and evaluations using alternative efficiency criteria.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the Bernoulli selection between a null output and an adjusted-coverage prediction set. Nonempty-output relaxation was already proposed in v1 Remark 5 and remains in v2 Remark 3.1; its new empirical instantiation does not establish a new general mechanism. The stability definition and underlying network architectures are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian-mixture and Gaussian simulations, ten regression datasets, and ImageNet validation classification task. The additions vary methods, output construction, bias magnitudes, or evaluation metrics within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds localized CP alongside VCP and PT-VCP in the stability comparison in Table 3. The classification relabeling from VCP/PT-VCP to RAPS/PT-RAPS is not a new comparator: v1 already identifies RAPS in the table captions and Appendix D.2.4.

E3.justification: New protocols include relaxed PT with epsilon = 0.01 and p = 0.96, fourfold larger regression biases, and ten classification efficiency criteria using 10,000 calibration examples and smoothed p-values. Localized-CP stability is evaluated across scale-estimator retraining. Appendix D.2.3 also corrects the stated CQR alpha from 1 to 0.1; unchanged Table 5 results do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 tests whether the phenomenon depends on exactly null outputs (Table 6), how stronger misspecification affects it (Table 7), and whether alternative efficiency criteria are also susceptible (Tables 9–10). Table 3 additionally examines stability in a practical stochastic CP pipeline. The original failure-case analysis and probability/bias sweeps remain.

E5.justification: The original five-seed, standard-error reporting is retained. New Tables 6–7 explicitly report means and standard deviations over five seeds, introducing a different dispersion-reporting practice. Neither an increased run count nor new significance testing is documented.

E6.justification: All original table scores are retained after matching renamed methods and renumbered tables. Substantial new results include localized-CP stability, relaxed-PT and stronger-bias outcomes, and PT-RAPS outperforming RAPS on seven of ten efficiency criteria. For example, the new high-bias BIKE comparison reports lengths 80.46 versus 77.29; this is an added setting, not a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: v2 changes the PT stability expression from p(1-p)(E[L])^2 to p(1-p)E[L^2], strengthens the concavity assumption to strict concavity, and revises the localized-CP limiting scale from 1 to a quantile ratio. It reformulates the first-order condition using averaged length G and adds a continuous-score success example with a proof in Appendix B.5. The merged coverage guarantees and renumbered secant condition largely retain existing mathematical content.

C1.justification: The headline contributions remain unchanged. However, v2 Introduction Remark 1.3 narrows the practical-relevance claim: it removes v1's assertion that cherry-picked local-scale estimators always make localized CP outperform VCP and explicitly avoids treating localized CP or APS/RAPS randomization as inherently PT-like.

C2.justification: v2 substantially qualifies the interpretation of algorithmic randomness: nonzero localized-CP stability is not evidence that its efficiency comes from PT-like behavior. It explains susceptibility beyond average length, interprets the nonempty-output experiment, and limits the alternative-criteria findings to empirical evidence. Conditional-coverage and misspecification statements receive clearer qualifications, while the new impact statement recommends complementary stability and utility evaluations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and documents settings for the new experiments, including perturbation magnitude, calibration size, p-value smoothing, and scale-estimator retraining. Existing architecture, optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size, and training-budget details remain unchanged. The new procedures are only briefly specified.

R1.justification: v2 adds Romano et al. (2020) for APS and Vovk et al. (2016) for efficiency criteria, and removes the Tyagi and Guo (2023) citation. Its relationship to localized CP is more carefully qualified. Numerous other reference changes are publication updates or consolidation of citations to the same works.

P1.justification: The overall Sections 1–5 and Appendices A–D structure remains. v2 rewrites selected interpretation passages, consolidates the coverage discussion, expands several proof explanations, standardizes RAPS terminology, and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement. Most surrounding exposition is retained.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes a two-column conference-format main text with new headers, typography, and float placement. Table 3 moves from the appendix into Section 4 and gains a comparator row; four new tables are added. All fifteen figures retain their graphical content but are resized or repositioned, including substantial rearrangement of appendix plots.

improvement.justification: v2 improves rigor through the corrected stability expression and concavity assumption, more accurate comparator labeling, and more careful claims about stochastic CP. The nonempty-output and alternative-efficiency experiments strengthen the existing argument. The gain remains limited by briefly specified new procedures and unresolved mathematical issues, including the unchanged sign inconsistency in the Gaussian failure-case proof in Appendix B.6.
